heading.en: The green scum in your pond is doing half the world's work
heading.kn: ಕೊಳದ ಹಸಿರು ಪಾಚಿ ಜಗತ್ತಿನ ಅರ್ಧ ಕೆಲಸ ಮಾಡುತ್ತಿದೆ

hook.en: Algae look like simple green slime, yet they carry out at least half of all the carbon dioxide fixation on earth.
hook.kn: ಶೈವಲಗಳು ಸರಳ ಹಸಿರು ಲೋಳೆಯಂತೆ ಕಂಡರೂ ಭೂಮಿಯ ಒಟ್ಟು ಇಂಗಾಲದ ಡೈಆಕ್ಸೈಡ್ ಸ್ಥಿರೀಕರಣದ ಕನಿಷ್ಠ ಅರ್ಧ ಭಾಗವನ್ನು ಮಾಡುತ್ತವೆ.

objectives.en: Compare artificial, natural and phylogenetic systems
Describe the form and reproduction of algae

narration.en: Algae look like simple green slime, yet they carry out at least half of all the carbon dioxide fixation on earth.

body.en: Early artificial systems, like that of Linnaeus, used a few superficial characters such as the androecium. Natural systems, like Bentham and Hooker's, used natural affinities including anatomy and embryology. Phylogenetic systems are based on evolutionary relationships. Numerical taxonomy uses computers and gives equal weight to all characters, cytotaxonomy uses chromosome number and behaviour, and chemotaxonomy uses chemical constituents.
body.kn: ಕೃತಕ ಪದ್ಧತಿ ಕೆಲವು ಮೇಲ್ನೋಟದ ಲಕ್ಷಣಗಳನ್ನು (ಉದಾ: ಪುಂಕೇಸರ) ಬಳಸಿತು. ನೈಸರ್ಗಿಕ ಪದ್ಧತಿ ಸಹಜ ಸಾಮ್ಯಗಳನ್ನು, ವಂಶಾವಳಿ ಪದ್ಧತಿ ವಿಕಾಸಾತ್ಮಕ ಸಂಬಂಧಗಳನ್ನು ಬಳಸುತ್ತದೆ.

title.en: On the board: Systems of classification and algae

say.en: Classification systems grew from a few characters to evolutionary relationships.
Artificial used few characters, like Linnaeus; natural used all affinities, like Bentham and Hooker; phylogenetic uses evolution.
Today numerical taxonomy, cytotaxonomy and chemotaxonomy add more evidence.
Algae fuse gametes in three ways. Isogamy: two similar gametes.
Oogamy: a large non-motile egg and a small motile male gamete, as in Volvox and Fucus.
Algae are useful: they fix half of the earth's carbon dioxide and give food, agar, algin and carrageen.

narration.en: Classification has changed over time. Sort these statements.

prompt.en: Sort each statement into the kind of classification it describes.
prompt.kn: ಪ್ರತಿ ಹೇಳಿಕೆಯನ್ನು ಅದು ವಿವರಿಸುವ ವರ್ಗೀಕರಣದ ಬಗೆಗೆ ವಿಂಗಡಿಸಿ.

text.en: A few superficial characters such as habit and colour
Vegetative and sexual characters given equal weight
Bentham and Hooker's classification of flowering plants
Uses natural affinities, including anatomy, embryology and phytochemistry
Assumes members of a taxon share a common ancestor
Numerical taxonomy: all characters given equal importance using computers
Chemotaxonomy: chemical constituents of the plant

explanation.en: Artificial systems used few characters; natural systems used many, including internal features; phylogenetic systems reflect evolution. Numerical taxonomy, cytotaxonomy and chemotaxonomy help settle difficult cases.

body.en: Algae are simple, thalloid, autotrophic, mostly aquatic plants with chlorophyll. They may be colonial like Volvox, filamentous like Ulothrix and Spirogyra, or massive like kelps. They reproduce vegetatively by fragmentation, asexually by zoospores, and sexually. Fusion of similar gametes is isogamy, of dissimilar gametes anisogamy, and of a large non-motile egg with a small motile male gamete oogamy, as in Volvox and Fucus.
body.kn: ಶೈವಲಗಳು ಹರಿತ್ತುಳ್ಳ ಸರಳ, ಥಾಲಸ್ ದೇಹದ, ಸ್ವಪೋಷಿ ಜಲಸಸ್ಯಗಳು. ಲೈಂಗಿಕ ಸಂತಾನೋತ್ಪತ್ತಿ: ಸಮಯುಗ್ಮನ, ಅಸಮಯುಗ್ಮನ ಮತ್ತು ಅಂಡಯುಗ್ಮನ (ವಾಲ್ವಾಕ್ಸ್, ಫ್ಯೂಕಸ್).

body.en: Algae fix about half of the earth's carbon dioxide and increase dissolved oxygen around them. Porphyra, Laminaria and Sargassum are eaten. Agar from Gelidium and Gracilaria is used to grow microbes and in jellies; algin comes from brown algae and carrageen from red algae. Chlorella is a protein-rich food supplement, used even by space travellers.
body.kn: ಶೈವಲಗಳು ಭೂಮಿಯ ಅರ್ಧದಷ್ಟು CO₂ ಸ್ಥಿರೀಕರಿಸುತ್ತವೆ. ಜೆಲಿಡಿಯಂ, ಗ್ರಾಸಿಲೇರಿಯಾದಿಂದ ಅಗರ್; ಕಂದು ಶೈವಲಗಳಿಂದ ಆಲ್ಜಿನ್; ಕ್ಲೋರೆಲ್ಲಾ ಪ್ರೋಟೀನ್‌ಯುಕ್ತ ಆಹಾರ ಪೂರಕ.

problem.en: In an alga, a large non-motile egg is fertilised by a small motile male gamete. Name the type of sexual reproduction and give two examples. How is it different from the case of Spirogyra?

steps.en: Unequal gametes where the female is large and non-motile is oogamy.
Spirogyra shows isogamy: its gametes are similar in size and non-flagellated.

narration.en: Let us work through this together. In an alga, a large non-motile egg is fertilised by a small motile male gamete. Name the type of sexual reproduction and give two examples. How is it different from the case of Spirogyra?
Class quiz. Discuss, raise hands, and the monitor taps the class answer.
